why: Fourth Wall Studios is the Japantown braindance studio run by producer Rachel Casich, used in vanilla for the Sinnerman / They Won't Go When I Go crucifixion recording. The street, gate, studio shell and most devices load in the base world; the studio's own quest-design section, its production crew and its door officer only exist while the side job runs. This proposal keeps the studio open for business in normal play: it loads the studio's quest-design section, restores the idle production crew (director, crew, actors, makeup, costumed extras) and one door guard, and clears the quest-era riot audio, protester barricade and mq303 street dressing so the venue looks like a working studio with no shoot in progress.

open_questions: Rachel Casich owns Fourth Wall Studios but has no idle spawn combination: vanilla only ever spawns her through #sq023_com_main_crew None/bd_start (with Joshua and Vasquez) or Deactivate nodes. Placing her would need a new single-entry spawn set or a cast-layer workspot; today the owner is missing from the venue.

The entry roster and character records of spawn set #sq023_com_bd_studio are not in the extracted data (only entry names from Deactivate nodes: crew, bd_director, actors, makeup01/02, soldier_one/two). The 'start' phase is inferred to be the relaxed pre-shoot state from its workspots; the tour should confirm the extras do not stand in a crucifixion tableau.

guard2 (Character.sq023_guard) is assumed to look like studio security rather than an NCPD officer; if the record is a police appearance, the gate would read as a permanent police detail and the entry should be dropped.

No access module, terminal or keycode for #sq023_dvc_bd_door appears in the quest data, so the door relies on the runtime policy's static-door unlock; the tour must confirm the player can enter without the quest.

The billboards can only be switched to the launched 'Passion' campaign, not to a neutral ad; if the baked default is the teaser campaign, the venue will carry quest marketing that cannot be removed with the available variants.

communities.why: One relaxed studio security guard on the street-side gate spot, so the entrance reads as a guarded corporate studio. The catalogue's spot map puts guard2 on base\workspots\common\ground\generic__stand_ground__guard__02.workspot at the gate (x -265, y 1110), the same cluster the quest cordon uses; the rest of the community (alert guard, the six NCPD officers) is quest cordon and is left out.

spawn_sets.why: The studio's own production crew in its pre-shoot idle state: bd_director, crew, actors, makeup01/02 and the two costumed soldier extras. Vanilla activates exactly this combo before the recording; the mapped start workspots are relaxed (director leaning/smoking, crew standing around, using a tablet or looking at products, extras standing or sitting in a chair), not a scene or combat state.

variant_toggles.why: Removes the protester/police barricade in front of the studio that the quest leaves baked on; normal play needs the street in front of the entrance clear.
Keeps the riot ambience off; the rioting crowd and its audio belong to the post-recording quest state and do not exist in our timeline.
Turns off the mq303 street dressing (the Lina & Toolina show pitch that mq303_consequences adds outside the studio). mq303 never runs in our timeline, so the pre-quest street look is var_mq303=0.

proximity_wait.why: The studio's own double entrance door (DoorControllerPS) in the always-loaded loc_sq023_braindance_studio_devices prefab; it sits on the only way in and streams with the location, so it is a reliable proximity anchor (not a workspot).
